_what_this_is: Archived record of an external citation that Round 03-A.5 and the A-line closure both depend on. Written from a live fetch of the arXiv abstract page so the dependency can be rechecked offline; it is evidence about what the cited source says, not agreement with it.
title_note: arXiv carries the misspelling 'Conjeture'. The subject bibliography silently corrects it to 'Conjecture'; that is a transcription difference, not a mismatch of work.
claimed_statement_in_the_subject: If a rational 2-adic integer has a divergent trajectory then liminf h(l)/l = ln2/ln3, where h counts the U symbols among the first l parity symbols.
abstract_sentence_supporting_it: if there is a rational 2-adic integer with a non-cyclic trajectory, then necessarily \underline{\lim}\;(\frac{h}{\ell})_{\ell=1}^{\infty}=\frac{\ln(2)}{\ln(3)}
verified: to a paper on the 3x+1 map on the 2-adic integers
whose abstract states the claimed liminf equality verbatim, in the same h/l notation the subject uses, for rational 2-adic integers with non-cyclic trajectories
not_verified: that the statement is numbered Theorem 1 inside the paper, as the subject calls it; only the abstract was read
peer review: no journal reference appeared on the listing, so it remains a preprint, which the subject bibliography itself flags
scope_note: Positive integers are rational 2-adic integers, and a positive-integer trajectory is non-cyclic exactly when it is unbounded, so the subject's specialisation to divergent positive-integer orbits is within the cited statement.
